title: Microsoft Agent Framework
tagline: Pick the rung, wire the pipeline, and keep long runs alive.
story: The team has picked a framework and still has to pick everything inside it. A plain agent, a Harness Agent and a graph workflow are three different promises about control, memory and recovery. This world shows how to choose the rung, wire the pipeline, pick the crew shape and keep a run alive across approvals and restarts.
oneLiner: Start with the lowest rung that meets the requirement, then climb only when a dial you can name forces you to.
youWillLearn: Choose between a plain function, an agent, a Harness Agent, a graph workflow and a workflow of agents using the dials that flip the choice
Place logic in agent, chat or function middleware, context providers or history providers, and predict the execution order
Decide where history lives (local, your store, service-managed) and see why that decides whether compaction works
Pick sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat or Magentic by task shape, cost and who should own the thread
Explain supersteps, checkpoints, human requests and checkpoint storage, including the pickle trust boundary
Separate background responses, background agents and durable agents, and read maturity labels honestly (checked 2026-10-13)
Defend a long-running, multi-agent, approval-gated design on the framework

flashcards.front: How does **Microsoft Agent Framework** relate to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen?
flashcards.back: It is the direct successor from the same teams. It joins Semantic Kernel's sessions, middleware and telemetry with AutoGen's agent and multi-agent patterns and adds graph workflows. AutoGen is in maintenance mode.

flashcards.front: Which Agent Framework parts are stable and which are not, as of 2026-10-13?
flashcards.back: Stable: core agents, graph workflows with checkpointing, orchestrations, declarative YAML. Beta or preview: Python devui, foundry-hosting, a2a, durabletask, azurefunctions packages and the .NET hosting, A2A and DevUI packages. Several features are experimental.

flashcards.front: State the docs' rule for choosing an agent, a workflow or neither.
flashcards.back: Agent: open-ended task, autonomous tool use. Workflow: well-defined steps, explicit order, several agents or functions to coordinate. If you can write a function to handle the task, do that instead of using an agent.

flashcards.front: What does the **Harness Agent** add, and is it a separate runtime?
flashcards.back: Not a runtime. It is a normal agent (`HarnessAgent` derives from `AIAgent`, `create_harness_agent()` returns an `Agent`) pre-wired with todos, plan and execute modes, file memory, standing approvals, per-call history persistence and telemetry.

flashcards.front: Name the three middleware kinds and what each wraps.
flashcards.back: Agent run middleware wraps a whole run. Function-calling middleware wraps each tool call. Chat-client middleware wraps each model call, including every tool-loop iteration (since 1.0.0rc5, 2026-03-19).

flashcards.front: What does `disable_tool_auto_approval=True` change in the Harness?
flashcards.back: It removes the tool-approval middleware (standing rules). It does not remove the approval requirement on the tool itself, because approval is a property of the tool.

flashcards.front: Where does compaction have no effect?
flashcards.back: On history held by a service: Foundry agents, Responses API with `store` on (the default) and Copilot Studio. Compaction applies only to agents that hold history in memory.

flashcards.front: Why are tool-call groups atomic in compaction?
flashcards.back: An assistant tool call and its results form one group that is never split, so the model never sees a call without its result. Strategies drop or collapse whole groups.

flashcards.front: What is a **superstep** in a workflow?
flashcards.back: One bulk-synchronous round: collect pending messages, route them over edges, run all target executors concurrently, wait at a barrier, queue new messages. A checkpoint is written at the end of each.

flashcards.front: What does a workflow checkpoint contain, and how do you resume?
flashcards.back: Executor state, pending messages for the next superstep, pending requests and responses, and shared state. Resume with `workflow.run(checkpoint_id=..., checkpoint_storage=...)`.

flashcards.front: What must stay identical for a rebuilt workflow to resume from a checkpoint?
flashcards.back: Topology and executor identities. In .NET give each agent a stable `ChatClientAgentOptions.Id` and keep its `Name`. Build fresh executor and agent instances per workflow.

flashcards.front: Why is checkpoint storage a trust boundary?
flashcards.back: File and Cosmos storage serialize non-JSON state with pickle behind a restricted unpickler. Never load checkpoints from untrusted or tampered sources. If pickle is unacceptable use in-memory storage or a custom `CheckpointStorage`.

flashcards.front: Handoff, agent-as-tool and group chat: who holds control?
flashcards.back: Handoff: mesh with no central orchestrator, the receiving agent owns the task. Agent-as-tool: control returns to the primary agent. Group chat: star, an orchestrator picks the speaker over a shared full history.

flashcards.front: Why try group chat before Magentic?
flashcards.back: Magentic adds a planning manager, a task ledger and re-plans, and the docs say it is untested outside the original Magentic-One design. Use it only when the path truly needs a plan.

Background responses: one provider request returns a continuation token you poll or use to resume a stream. Background agents (experimental): a parent delegates tasks to child agents, there is no cancel tool, and in-flight work is lost on restart.

flashcards.front: What does the Durable Extension add?
flashcards.back: Persisted sessions, workflow checkpointing, resume after failure, and pauses for human input that use no compute or tokens. Runs on Azure Functions or your own compute. Beta in Python and preview in .NET as of 2026-10-13.

flashcards.front: What do Foundry hosted agents give an Agent Framework agent?
flashcards.back: A containerized, managed host with the Responses protocol (OpenAI-compatible `/responses`, recommended) and the Invocations protocol, a persisted `$HOME` and files, and an Entra identity per agent. The service is GA while the framework hosting package is Beta or preview.

flashcards.front: Two migration facts that bite Semantic Kernel and AutoGen users?
flashcards.back: Semantic Kernel agent classes collapse into `ChatClientAgent`. AutoGen's `AssistantAgent` is single-turn unless `max_tool_iterations` is raised, while the Agent Framework `Agent` is multi-turn by default.

glossary.def: Microsoft's open-source framework for agents and workflows in .NET, Python and (in preview) Go. The direct successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen.
A normal agent pre-wired for long multi-step work: todos, plan and execute modes, file memory, standing approvals, per-call history persistence and telemetry. Not a separate runtime.
A graph of executors joined by edges that runs in supersteps. It gives explicit order, fan-out, checkpoints and human requests. A built workflow is immutable.
A node in a workflow: a class with `@handler` methods or a function. It sends messages downstream with `ctx.send_message()` and yields workflow output with `ctx.yield_output()`.
One bulk-synchronous round of a workflow: route pending messages, run target executors concurrently, wait at a barrier. Checkpoints align with supersteps.
A snapshot written at the end of a superstep: executor state, pending messages, pending requests and responses, and shared state. It lets a run resume after a restart.
Code that wraps a whole agent run. Function middleware wraps each tool call and chat middleware wraps each model call. All three can short-circuit.

A component that runs around each invocation (`before_run`, `after_run`) to add instructions, messages, tools or middleware. One instance serves every session, so per-session data lives in `session.state`.
A component that loads and stores the transcript. Configure one with `load_messages=True`. Audit copies use `load_messages=False`.
The state container for a conversation: `session_id`, an optional `service_session_id` and a mutable `state` dict that providers share. Sessions are agent and service specific.
Shrinking locally held history with truncation, a sliding window, tool-result collapse, summarization or a pipeline. Message groups stay atomic. It has no effect on service-managed history.
A mesh of agents with no central orchestrator. Control moves through handoff tool calls and the receiving agent owns the task.
Group chat shape with a planning manager based on Magentic-One. It keeps a task ledger and limits rounds, stalls and plan resets.
A single provider request that returns a continuation token. You poll with it or use it to resume an interrupted stream.
Durable Task based hosting for agents and workflows on Azure Functions or your own compute. Persists sessions and checkpoints and waits for humans without using compute.

claims.text: Agent Framework 1.0 was announced for .NET and Python on 2026-04-03; at GA the stable parts were agents, graph workflows with checkpointing, orchestrations, declarative YAML and MCP.
Python package agent-framework 1.21.0 was uploaded to PyPI on 2026-10-08 and requires Python 3.10 or later.
The Go SDK is in public preview and has no packaged Harness, no declarative agents and no Foundry hosting package.
The docs rule: if you can write a function to handle the task, do that instead of using an AI agent.
HarnessAgent derives from AIAgent and Python create_harness_agent() returns an Agent; it is not a separate runtime.

Harness defaults on: function invocation with an iteration limit, per-service-call history persistence, todo tracking, plan and execute modes, standing tool approvals, OpenTelemetry. Opt-in: shared file access, background agents, shell execution, looping. Compaction is on only when token limits or a custom strategy are supplied.
The Harness default tool-approval middleware requires the same AgentSession across approval round trips.
Semantic Kernel v1.x is supported for at least one year after Agent Framework is GA, which with GA on 2026-04-03 gives about 2027-04 at the earliest.
Mixed-scope middleware with agent middleware [A1, A2] and run middleware [R1, R2] executes A1, A2, R1, R2, agent, R2, R1, A2, A1.
Since 1.0.0rc5 (2026-03-19) chat middleware runs per model call, including every tool-loop iteration, not once per run.
Compaction applies only to agents holding history in memory and has no effect on Foundry agents, Responses API with store on, or Copilot Studio.
Compaction message groups are atomic: a tool call group (assistant tool calls plus results) is never split.
Setting disable_tool_auto_approval=True removes the approval middleware but does not remove the approval requirement on the tool.
Configure only one history provider with load_messages=True; require_per_service_call_history_persistence=True raises an error when the run is bound to a service-managed conversation.
OpenAI resp_* and conv_* ids are scoped to the API key or project, so a service id from a client must be mapped to your own store and checked against the user or tenant.

Handoff is a mesh with no central orchestrator, supports only Agent with local tool execution, and is interactive by default; autonomous mode is experimental with a .NET default of 50 turns per agent.
Magentic plan review is off by default in Python (enable_plan_review=False) and on by default in .NET (RequirePlanSignoff true).
The Magentic docs warn that its performance outside the original Magentic-One design is untested.
The default concurrent aggregator returns one AgentResponse with one assistant message per participant; only the aggregator output is terminal unless intermediate_output_from is set.
Python 1.2.2 (2026-04-29) standardized orchestration terminal output as AgentResponse, so workflow.as_agent() returns only the final answer.
A workflow checkpoint is created at the end of each superstep and holds executor state, pending messages, pending requests and responses, and shared state.
Python 1.13.0 (2026-07-30) also writes an entry checkpoint before the first superstep and when request responses arrive.
File checkpoint storage uses a restricted unpickler since python-1.0.1 (2026-04-09) and Cosmos storage since python-1.1.0 (2026-04-21); extra types are allowed with allowed_checkpoint_types.
In a fan-out where one branch is a chain and another is one slow executor, the chain stalls at the superstep barrier.
Pending human requests are stored in checkpoints and re-emitted on restore; resume with workflow.run(responses=...), optionally with checkpoint_id in the same call.
The Durable Extension pauses for human input without using compute or tokens; its Python packages are Beta and its .NET packages are preview as of 2026-10-13.
Background agents use six delegation tools, have no cancel tool, and in-flight work does not survive a restart; the feature is experimental.
Foundry hosted agents support the Responses and Invocations protocols; the hosting service is GA while agent-framework-foundry-hosting is Beta.
No general-purpose durable AgentSessionStore ships for self-hosting, so you supply session persistence.
